title: Adaptive Fleet Dimmer — Console scaling sliders, live throughput dashboard, and change chronicle
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a 'dimmer' style control in the Console Fleet Controls panel that lets operators smoothly adjust target throughput (rps/tokens-per-second) across a fleet. Combine the slider UI with a live throughput heatmap and a compact change chronicle (time-ordered audit feed) so operators can adjust capacity quickly and trace who made changes. Includes UX for per-operator presets, temporary overrides, and an automatic rollback trigger when latency SLOs degrade.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Slider controls persist as fleet presets and apply immediately to dedicated capacity pools. 2) Live throughput dashboard updates within 8s of control changes and shows per-shard and aggregate RPS/TPM. 3) Change chronicle records actor, delta, reason, and links to PR or incident; supports filtering by user and time range. 4) Temporary overrides auto-expire and are visible in the audit timeline. 5) End-to-end tests for RBAC (operator vs viewer) pass.
qa_notes: Test staging with synthetic traffic generator (throughput-sim v0.4) to validate slider granularity at 1%, 5%, and 10% steps. Verify metric propagation to Grafana and alerting rules. Confirm change chronicle entries show correct actor display name and immutable timestamp.
risks: large fleets might exhibit propagation lag >8s on older infra
audit log retention policy may increase storage costs
mitigations: apply server-side sequencing with optimistic concurrency control
add canary rollout for slider sync to 10% of fleets
compress audit entries older than 90 days and backfill via batch job
notes: Requested by Platform SRE during enterprise onboarding call; priority raised due to need for manual overrides in incidents.
Design review 2026-03-05: prefer slider with numeric input fallback for precise targets.
Engineering spike showed kernel scheduling needs minor refactor to accept dynamic throughput caps.
